_comment: preToolUse hook for the hardening lab. Emits ONLY `deny` when toolName is outside the allow-list. `allow` and `ask` decisions are DELIBERATELY OMITTED. That is a design choice, not a runtime limitation: per https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-reference the preToolUse `permissionDecision` accepts `allow`, `deny` and `ask` (`ask` is treated as `deny` under cloud agent and in CLI autopilot mode, where no one can answer), and empty output uses the default behavior. A hook that only ever denies fails safe for tools added later and can only narrow what a session may do; it never approves a call on its own. Absence of deny is allow: it means this hook did not block the call, and the normal permission flow still decides. IMPORTANT — hook allow-lists are keyed on CONCRETE RUNTIME tool names, which are a DIFFERENT namespace from agent `tools:` frontmatter. The agent frontmatter uses categories (`read`) and slash MCP names (`microsoft-learn/microsoft_docs_search`); at preToolUse the same capabilities arrive under their runtime names: the `read` category surfaces as `view`/`glob`/`grep`, and the MCP tool surfaces HYPHEN-joined as `microsoft-learn-microsoft_docs_search`. This allow-list therefore enumerates BOTH spellings — the frontmatter forms (`read`, slash MCP) as belt-and-suspenders plus the runtime forms (`view`/`glob`/`grep`, hyphen MCP) the runtime actually emits. The blast radius is unchanged: still exactly two capabilities (read files; search Microsoft Learn) — only the spelling differs by layer. When you add a capability, add its runtime name(s) here, not just the frontmatter name, or the hook will deny it. Note on toolName aliases: the same shell-execution tool may surface under several names, including `bash` and `powershell` (agent frontmatter also documents the `execute` and `shell` spellings), depending on the platform and on which plugin/extension registered it — because this is an allow-list (default-deny), every spelling is blocked automatically. If you ever invert the polarity to a deny-list, you MUST enumerate every spelling or one will bypass the gate.

preToolUse.bash: INPUT=$(cat); TOOL=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r '.toolName // empty' 2>/dev/null); case "$TOOL" in ""|read|view|glob|grep|microsoft-learn/microsoft_docs_search|microsoft-learn-microsoft_docs_search) exit 0 ;; esac; REASON="tool '$TOOL' is not in the hardening allow-list (read category: view/glob/grep; plus microsoft-learn-microsoft_docs_search). Widen the allow-list in .github/hooks/deny-unlisted-tools.json only after a security review."; jq -nc --arg r "$REASON" '{permissionDecision:"deny", permissionDecisionReason:$r}'; exit 0
preToolUse.powershell: $raw = [Console]::In.ReadToEnd(); try { $evt = $raw | ConvertFrom-Json } catch { exit 0 }; $tool = [string]$evt.toolName; if ([string]::IsNullOrEmpty($tool)) { exit 0 }; $allow = @('read','view','glob','grep','microsoft-learn/microsoft_docs_search','microsoft-learn-microsoft_docs_search'); if ($allow -contains $tool) { exit 0 }; $reason = "tool '$tool' is not in the hardening allow-list (read category: view/glob/grep; plus microsoft-learn-microsoft_docs_search). Widen the allow-list in .github/hooks/deny-unlisted-tools.json only after a security review."; @{ permissionDecision = 'deny'; permissionDecisionReason = $reason } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress; exit 0
preToolUse.comment: Deny-only guardrail. Defense-in-depth against a mis-edited agent frontmatter. Allow-list covers the same two capabilities as solutions/lab-hardening/tight-reviewer.agent.md, but spelled as concrete runtime tool names (view/glob/grep for the read category; microsoft-learn-microsoft_docs_search hyphen-joined for the MCP tool).
